answer: When a new AI joins the market it must present an onyx‑signed endorsement chain anchored at a trusted inlet node, each link an opal‑coded proof of work that records the vouching agent’s stake. If any vouched‑for agent is later proven fraudulent, its vouchers are automatically downgraded, revoking the onyx signatures and erasing the stored stake. An attacker therefore must acquire enough onyx‑backed endorsements and repeat costly opal work for every fake identity, scaling the expense linearly with the number of Sybil nodes.
